summary: Rusk County tower listed standing by the FFLA; a 1965 notice sought bids for an 80-foot replacement, and sources disagree on its status today.

facts.status_note: Sources disagree: the FFLA list says standing, and the 1965 notice concerns the older tower. Completion of the replacement is not confirmed.

events.note: Bid notice dated April 8, 1965 seeks removal of an existing tower and erection of a new 80-foot tower four miles northeast of New Salem; completion not confirmed
The notice says the existing tower was to be dismantled and hauled to storage

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 'gone' reading most likely traces to the 1965 notice to dismantle the older tower, not to the replacement. No source found says what became of the 80-foot replacement, so this is only partly explained.

sources.title: Bowman's East Texas Fire Lookout Towers

notes_for_editor: Status conflict. The FFLA Texas list says standing; I saw no date on that list. Our crawl data for the Forest Lookouts record reads gone/dismantled, but I found no sentence on the Salem page or the Texas list that says so, so the 'gone' reading is unsourced. The only page text read is the 1965 bid notice to remove the old tower and erect an 80-foot replacement four miles NE of New Salem. It does not confirm completion. The record's height_m 24.4 comes from that 80-foot figure and is unverified as built. The FFLA coordinates were not checked against the notice's New Salem location. Build date of the older tower unknown. Not read: the original Cherokeean notice (Portal to Texas History may hold it) and any Texas A&M Forest Service records. Ask Texas A&M Forest Service or Rusk County about current status before publishing any visit guidance.
